contexts.text: The voices or sounds of such instruments...

Angels and Spirits distinguish sounds according to differences as to good and truth, not only those of songs and instruments, but also those of voices; and they admit none but those which are in accord, so that there may be a concordance of sounds, and consequently of instruments, with the nature and essence of the good and truth.
If man did not know by the discriminations of sound learned by use from infancy, and did not see the speaker at a distance, he would believe that he was speaking close to his ear.
There was an image of the deceit in every tone of the voice.
As I heard the men sonorously, so did I hear the Spirits. AC 4652:2. HH 248. SE 5589.
Each Society, and Spirit, can be distinguished from others... by the tones. SE 2181.
The speech of celestial Spirits cannot easily flow into articulate sounds or words with man; for it cannot be fitted to a word in which there is anything sounding harshly...
A speech... as if to the tone and sound of threshing.
Some speak with a raucous or cracked sound.
The sound of those advancing... was heard by them variously; by some as the sound of armed horsemen...
A threefold sound of murmurs heard.
Truth without good... is only a sounding something. AC 2689:4.
I heard a sonorous gyre, grosser than usual... it was from gentiles.
Under Ear, see this reference.
A whisper is heard more noisily than open speech.
I heard a soft sound, angelically sweet. SE 1176.
This is manifestly heard from the sound of their speech. AC 6616.
Like the difference between the extension of sound, and that of light.
Ideas are sonorous there.
Speech in Mars is not sonorous...
Speech in Jupiter is not so sonorous as with us.
(Correspondence of sounds with affections.) Explained.
(The speech of the Spirits of Jupiter) does not terminate in what is sonorous...
The spiritual speak sonorously... but not so the celestial... SE 5521.
The sound as the sound of great waters () = the quality of Divine truth in Heaven.
Like a sound on high, where the atmosphere is purer, which is tacit; but when it descends to where the atmosphere is grosser, it is greater, and more noisy.

The sound from bells is here called a voice; elsewhere the sounds and clangs from trumpets and thunders are so called, and by them are signified Divine truths. The sounds of musical instruments = like things; those which give out a stridulous and discrete sound = spiritual Divine truths; those which give out a continuous sound, celestial Divine truths.

For the sound whether of speech, singing, or shouting, proceeds from the interior affection and thought, which are in the sound, and are also perceived by those who pay attention... and in the other life so exquisitely, that the quality of anyone as to his interiors is perceived by Angels from the sound of one word. HH 269:2.

(In the Fourth Earth) they have not articulate speech... yet it ceases in what is sonorous... From this sonorousness, modified by ideas, discourse is perceived more fully... for the general affection which is in the sound of man's speech... gives an interior apperception. AC 10709:end.
They hear from the very sound of the speech whether it is from the heart.
Angelic speech... is uttered and heard equally sonorously...
The sound of speech (in Heaven) corresponds to their affection...
Spirits have spoken with me far off equally as sonorously as when near.
What the Angels do not express by their words, they supply in the tone, in which there is an affection of the Things in their order...
A (novitiate) Spirit has a like face and a like sound of speech.
From the mere sound of the words in the ear...
The Angels know a man's love from the sound of his speech; and his wisdom from the articulation of the sound. DLW 427:3.
Affection in thought is circumstanced as is sound in speech...
Like a sound continually in the ear.

Sound is not anything unless there is something in it which distinguishes it. Sound, moreover, corresponds to the affection with man; and as there is always something in it which distinguishes it, therefore from the sound of a man when speaking is known the affection of his love; and from the variation of it, which is speech, his thought. Hence it is that merely from the sound of one speaking the wiser Angels perceive his life's loves, together with some of the affections which are derivations.
(Thus) the internal lies hidden in the tone, etc., of the external.
The sound corresponds to the affection, and the speech to the thought.

The first changes and variations of the state and form of the sound take place in the lungs; the second in the trachea and larynx; the third in the glottis by means of the various apertures of its orifice; the fourth in the tongue by its various applications to the palate and teeth; and the fifth in the lips by their various forms, (Thus) the mere changes and variations of the state of the organic forms, continued successively, produce sounds and their articulations, which are speech and song. (The correspondence of this with the production of affections and thoughts.)
When we looked down from Heaven into the world, we saw nothing, but only heard sounds, for the most part unharmonious.
I heard a sound as of a mill.
For affection sounds, and thought speaks.

By voice is meant sound, and every sound corresponds to an affection which is of love, because it originates thence. It is from this that the sounds of harps, etc., from their correspondence, signify affections. Explained.

Speech is nothing but the form of sound; (and) sound corresponds to affection, and speech to thought; therefore affection sounds, and thought speaks... Take away the sound from speech, and how much speech will there be? (So with thought when affection is taken away from it.)
Origin of the harsher sound [of the voice] with men. CL 218.
The life of wisdom from the wife was heard in the sound (of her husband's voice).
The sound of the speech is from the affection of the will...
In the Spiritual World, a variety and commixture of affections is perceived in a sound distinctly.
The internal affections (of Spirits and Angels) are perceived in the sound of their speech.
Without this separation (of the understanding from the will) man could only sound his affection.
They utter falsities... in a tone emulative of spiritual affection...
The sound of the voice and speech of man is heard as only a simple sound; yet when Angels hear it, they perceive in it all the affections of his love... TCR 593:end. TCR 778.
Sound, which is an activity of the atmosphere, is not creatable; but its organ is.
From their tones and replies I gathered...
On a spiritual idea... from the sound of the words.
Where a bell sounded every hour... and I did not attend to the sound of the bell, I could never know that it had sounded...
Under Instrument, see this reference.
The sound (of speech) is from all the consonant osseous system, and that of the body, according to the affinities with the proximates.
Indications of two kinds: from the sound, and from the idea. The sound has its differences ad indefinitum...
Spirits who sounded together as many...
Speech by ideas also is sonorous.
Sound corresponds to affections; and in Heaven affections are perceived from sounds...
Discrete sounds excite affections of truth... and continuous sounds, affections of good.
Various kinds of sounds (in the Word).
All affection, being of love, when it falls into sound, sounds in accordance with itself...
For there are affections which produce varieties of sounds with men...
The Voluntary presents itself by sounds.
Sounds, in the world, increase when they descend from heights... whence come thunders. (The correspondence of this.)
Every affection, whether of grief or joy, expresses itself by sounds.
Sounds enter the will and the affection.
The affection itself is expressed by the sound of the speech.
If the affection of good were to descend into discourse, it would not speak, but would only sound.
When man becomes a Spirit... the sound of his speech is the sound of his affection.
By the angels of the Third Heaven, a man's quality is Known from the sound of his speech, etc.
From the Celestial Kingdom there are not heard words of speech, but sounds. Explained.
A beast, which has no thought from the understanding, but only knowledge from affection, can do nothing but sound, and vary the sound of its affection according to its appetite.

In the speech of men there are two things together: the sound, and its articulation into words. The sound is of the affection of the will; and the articulation of the sound is of the thought of the understanding... and the affection is known from the sound, and the thought from the words, which are the articulations of the sound.

The sound of the speech of the Angels in the higher parts of Heaven is heard below variously, for it increases as it progresses... The sound of the spiritual Angels is heard as the sound of roaring waters; and the sound of the celestial Angels as the sound of thunders.

5. Sounds which derive little from the understanding are the sounds of singing and of music; those which derive more from the understanding are the interior sounds of speech; and those which derive still more from it are the exterior sounds of speech... There is a correspondence of sounds and speech with the life of the will... and of the understanding; (for) from the sound may be perceived the quality of the affection... The correspondence of the sound itself is with the general affection of love in the understanding; the correspondence of the variations of the sound, such as are those of singing and music, is with the variations of the affections which are from the love of the will in the understanding; the correspondence of the variations of sound which derive very little from the understanding, is with perception; that of those which derive more is with the variation of perceptions; and that of those which derive much, is with thought and its variations.
There is a twofold form of sound; one of song, and the other of speech. In like manner with the affection of truth from good.
